results.title: AI-generated sensors open new paths for early cancer detection
results.content: Caption: Nanoparticles coated with AI-generated peptides can act as sensors that signal if cancer-linked proteases are present in the body. Nanoparticles coated with AI-generated peptides can act as sensors that signal if cancer-linked proteases are present in the body. “We’re focused on ultra-sensitive detection in diseases like the early stages of cancer, when the tumor burden is small, or early on in recurrence after surgery,” says Sangeeta Bhatia, the John and Dorothy Wilson Professor of Health Sciences and Technology and of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science at MIT, and a member of MIT’s Koch Institute for Integrative Cancer Research and the Institute for Medical Engineering and Science (IMES). In their new study, the researchers moved beyond the traditional trial-and-error process by developing a novel AI system, named CleaveNet, to design peptide sequences that could be cleaved efficiently and specifically by target proteases of interest. Such a resource could further accelerate research in early cancer detection, protease biology, and AI models for peptide design.
